title: 4.3 A 0.36nW, 820µm², 32kHz Conduction-Angle-Adaptive Crystal Oscillator in 28nm CMOS for Real-Time Clock Applications
problem: 32.768kHz crystal oscillators (XOs) for real-time clocks consume 10-100nW, and pulse-injection XOs (PIXOs) achieving sub-nW power still require separate start-up circuits and face robustness challenges under interference.
motivation: Battery-powered IoT sensor nodes require ultra-low-power always-on oscillators with good frequency stability; higher power consumption forces longer communication guard times, wasting additional energy in transceivers.
method: The crystal oscillator, built in 28nm CMOS, injects tiny pulses of energy at adaptively timed moments in the oscillation cycle (Class-C-like operation, where transistors conduct only during a narrow window). The timing of these conduction-angle pulses adjusts automatically to match the oscillator's state, allowing it to start itself without a separate start-up circuit. This eliminates the need for added control logic while providing robust oscillation that resists interference.
key_novelty: By automatically adjusting the conduction angle (the phase when transistors are active in each cycle), the oscillator starts itself without needing a separate start-up circuit.
